title: Patricia Duvic
dek_or_short_description: Close friend. Frequent personal correspondence during 1972–1973 about life experiences and private matters.
body_markdown:
Patricia Duvic (sometimes spelled Patrice) was a close friend to whom PKD wrote frequently during 1972–1973, sharing personal details and the texture of his daily life. Unlike some of his more intellectual correspondents, with Duvic the emphasis was on personal connection — what was happening, how he was feeling, the substance of lived experience.

The letters to Duvic suggest someone he trusted with intimate details. In the context of PKD's chaotic personal life during this period — with marriages dissolving, paranoia mounting, and metaphysical experiences consuming his attention — Duvic represented a stable point of human connection.

What the letters do not reveal is what Duvic gave back to this relationship, or what her own life and concerns might have been. Like so many correspondents in the archive, she is known primarily through PKD's side of the exchange. Yet her presence in his letter-writing pattern is unmistakable: someone who mattered enough to receive frequent, personal communication during a difficult time.
summary: Patricia Duvic (1972–1973+), close friend. Frequent personal correspondence about life experiences and private matters.
